q: The weight of body is the ____ acting on it which gives its acceleration when it is falling.
e: The weight of body is the force of gravity acting on it which gives its acceleration when it is falling. Force of gravity here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The acceleration due to the earth's attraction is called ____ and it is represented by the symbol g.
e: The acceleration due to the earth's attraction is called acceleration due to gravity and it is represented by the symbol g. Acceleration due to gravity here means how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.
In FPS system, $g = 32 \text{ ft s}^{-2}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $g = 32 \text{ ft s}^{-2}$.

q: The attracting force of the earth acting on a body is defined as the ____ of the body.
e: The attracting force of the earth acting on a body is defined as the weight of the body. Weight here means the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: The gravitational force acting on the body (or) the weight of the body is found to be ____.
e: The gravitational force acting on the body (or) the weight of the body is found to be $w=mg$. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: Weight is a ____ and is directed toward the center of the Earth.
e: Weight is a vector and is directed toward the center of the Earth. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: Mass is the ____ in a body.
e: Mass is the quantity of matter in a body. Quantity of matter here means anything that has mass and occupies space.
Mass is also a measure of inertia. Measure of inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion.

q: The mass of a body defined from this point of view is called ____ while the mass defined by $m = \frac{W}{g}$ is called gravitational mass.
e: The mass of a body defined from this point of view is called inertial mass while the mass defined by $m = \frac{W}{g}$ is called gravitational mass. Inertial mass here means the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: Wherever a body may be, there is no change in the value of the ____ of the body.
e: Wherever a body may be, there is no change in the value of the mass of the body. Mass here means the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: But the ____ of the body can change.
e: But the weight of the body can change. Weight here means the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: Mass is a ____ and always a constant.
e: Mass is a scalar and always a constant. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. A scalar is done once you have the size and the unit.
